title: New MSFS Marketplace Addons! Cold War Tempelhof & City Landmarks Drop
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator marketplace just loaded up a phenomenal collection of diverse European destinations this week! Whether you want to land at a rugged island cliff runway, tackle challenging short-field approaches in coastal Scotland, or explore beautifully updated mainline gateways across France and Germany, there is an adventure waiting for your virtual hangar.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we split today's major releases into two logical groups to see which environments genuinely deserve a spot on your virtual flight logs:

✈️ EUROPEAN HISTORIC AVIATION & CITY SCENERY: We kick things off in Cold War Germany with Berlin Tempelhof 1970s (EDDI) by Sundowner Sim. This historic recreation takes us back to when Berlin was split, featuring 1970s era-accurate Pan Am Boeing 727s, BEA Viscounts, USAF transports, and iconic Lockheed U-2 spy planes surrounding the curved terminal building. Next, we fly over to Landmarks Frankfurt by DFFlyerDirect, bringing Germany's financial capital to life with over 200 handcrafted downtown buildings, custom night lighting, and a dense cityscape nickname "Mainhattan."

🌏 US REGIONAL & GENERAL AVIATION AIRFIELD DESTINATIONS: Next, we head across the Atlantic to Florida for Fernandina Beach (KFHB) by Spinoza, located on Amelia Island. Featuring a main terminal designed to mimic the iconic F4U Corsair and detailed surrounding static aircraft, it's a great coastal destination. Finally, we travel to Utah to explore Roosevelt Municipal Airport (74V) by UK2000 Scenery, sitting above 5,000 feet with custom ground textures and fully detailed hanger interiors (just remember to download the free UK2000 common library first!).

Which of these environments are you adding to your flight routes first? Are you planning to turn back the clock at Tempelhof, or will you be weaving through the skyscrapers of Frankfurt? Let me know in the comments below!

If this structured marketplace breakdown helped you plan your next route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism and scenery updates!
